tasks.prompt: A seasonal disinfection review finds free chlorine residuals collapse in one pressure district every July while plant effluent residuals stay strong.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment utility record. Steady operation unless noted. Archived plant, laboratory, and management records are available for review.

evidence.label: Plant effluent residual is 1.2 mg/L in July, the same as in May.
District D samples fall to 0.1 mg/L in July, while other districts hold 0.7 to 0.9 mg/L.
District D includes a ground storage tank with July turnover of 9 days, versus 2 days in May.
Bench decay testing on July tank water shows high decay matching sediment and biofilm found at tank inspection.
A trial with daily tank cycling and cleaning restored District D residuals to 0.7 mg/L the next July period.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Long July storage time and tank condition in District D consume the residual after water leaves the plant
The plant under doses chlorine every July
All districts lose residual equally in warm weather
Tank turnover has no effect on residual in District D

inference.explanation: Effluent residual is steady and other districts hold theirs, so plant dosing is not the cause. The affected district alone has long turnover and a decay prone tank, and cycling plus cleaning restored its residuals.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the district cause?

options.label: Archived other district residual log
Archived District D tank turnover and bench decay results paired with district residual trends
Archived plant effluent residual log alone

nextClue.explanation: The correct record directly tests the supported explanation against the alternatives.

clueText.nc-a: Other districts held residuals, so the cause is local to District D.
clueText.nc-b: Turnover rose to 9 days, bench decay matched, and the cycling trial restored residuals.
clueText.nc-c: Effluent residuals were strong, ruling out plant dosing.

evidence.label: Raising alum dose increased total organic carbon removal from 32 percent to 48 percent in paired jar and plant trials.
Finished water alkalinity fell from 82 to 44 mg/L as CaCO3 and pH fell by 0.5 units at the higher dose.
Sludge solids production rose 38 percent at the higher dose in the plant trial.
A mid dose trial achieved 44 percent organic removal with alkalinity at 64 mg/L and a 18 percent sludge increase.
Disinfection byproduct results were lowest at the mid and high doses and highest at the current dose.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The highest dose is best on every measure that matters
Alkalinity and sludge do not change with alum dose
The current dose gives the lowest byproducts
The mid dose gives most of the organic and byproduct benefit with materially lower alkalinity loss and sludge growth than the high dose

inference.explanation: The high dose wins only on organic removal, while alkalinity, pH, and sludge all worsen, and byproducts were highest at the current dose. The mid dose captures most removal and byproduct benefit with smaller side effects, which the paired trials quantify.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the mid dose balance?

options.label: Archived paired dose trial summary for organic removal, alkalinity, sludge, and byproducts
Archived alum delivery log
Archived raw water colour log

nextClue.explanation: The correct record directly tests the supported explanation against the alternatives.

clueText.nc-a: The summary shows the mid dose near the high dose on removal and byproducts with half the sludge increase.
clueText.nc-b: Deliveries show use, not trial performance.
clueText.nc-c: Colour alone does not capture alkalinity or sludge effects.

All eight filter media beds failed at the same time

Archived run time, raw turbidity, and clean bed headloss trends for the filter fleet

clueText.nc-b: Backwash recovered headloss fully, so the pump log does not show failure.

Archived hardness results alone

clueText.nc-b: Total dose does not show the Well 3 idle period loss.

nextClue.explanation: The correct record directly tests the supported explanation against the alternatives.

clueText.nc-a: Scales were calibrated and hauling was not the gap.
clueText.nc-b: Dose totals were part of the correct input side.
clueText.nc-c: Recomputing with the current area closes the balance from 30 percent to 4 percent.

tasks.prompt: Compliance sampling program design is reviewed after the utility population and sample site map changed with a new subdivision.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment utility record. Steady operation unless noted. Archived plant, laboratory, and management records are available for review.

evidence.label: The new subdivision adds 4000 residents in the far pressure zone, which currently holds 2 of the utility 30 routine bacteriological sites.
Site selection records show the 2 far zone sites were chosen when the zone had 800 residents.
Regulatory site distribution expectations scale with population served across zones in the utility sampling plan criteria.
A revised site plan adding 4 far zone sites in a trial quarter produced results consistent with the existing sites and no adverse findings.
Sampling staff capacity covers the added sites within existing routes per the trial records.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The site network no longer matches population distribution, and the trial supports adding far zone sites to restore representative coverage
Two sites remain representative regardless of population growth
The trial added sites and found adverse results in the new zone
Sampling capacity prevents any added sites

inference.explanation: The far zone grew five fold while its site count stayed fixed, and criteria scale sites with population. The trial added sites with consistent, non adverse results and within existing capacity, contradicting the capacity and adverse claims.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the redesign need?

options.label: Archived sampling staff roster alone
Archived site distribution by zone population before and after the subdivision, with trial site results
Archived original site selection memo

nextClue.explanation: The correct record directly tests the supported explanation against the alternatives.

clueText.nc-a: The roster alone does not show route capacity, which the trial proved.
clueText.nc-b: Far zone population rose from 800 to 4800 with sites fixed at 2, and trial sites performed consistently.
clueText.nc-c: The old memo reflects the old population.

tasks.prompt: Treated water storage inspection findings are prioritized after divers inspect three ground reservoirs in one program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment utility record. Steady operation unless noted. Archived plant, laboratory, and management records are available for review.

evidence.label: Reservoir 1 shows coating failure and light corrosion at the roof hatch with a damaged hatch seal.
Reservoir 2 shows sediment depth of 0.3 m but intact coating and seals throughout.
Reservoir 3 shows a cracked vent screen and bird evidence inside the vent plenum.
Water quality samples from all three reservoirs meet targets, with Reservoir 3 showing the highest heterotrophic counts of the three.
All three reservoirs are the same age and construction.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Reservoir 2 sediment is the top priority because it is the largest measured quantity
All findings carry equal priority because the reservoirs are the same age
Water quality results prove none of the findings matter
Reservoir 3 vent breach is the first priority because it is an open contamination pathway, ahead of coating and sediment maintenance items

inference.explanation: A cracked vent with bird evidence is a direct entry pathway, and Reservoir 3 already shows the highest counts, while coating and sediment are maintenance conditions without an open pathway. Meeting targets today does not erase an open pathway finding.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the vent priority?

options.label: Archived dive inspection reports with photographs for the three reservoirs and their sample comparison
Archived reservoir age and construction records
Archived sediment depth measurements alone

nextClue.explanation: The correct record directly tests the supported explanation against the alternatives.

clueText.nc-a: Photos show an open vent pathway with bird evidence and Reservoir 3 has the highest counts.
clueText.nc-b: Same age does not rank pathway risk.
clueText.nc-c: Sediment depth is a maintenance measure, not a contamination pathway.

tasks.prompt: A source protection review examines a fuel storage site inside the intake protection zone after its inspection by the utility.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment utility record. Steady operation unless noted. Archived plant, laboratory, and management records are available for review.

evidence.label: The site stores heating fuel in a single wall tank installed before current standards, 180 m from the intake.
Secondary containment is absent and the fill area drains toward a ditch connected to the source creek.
The property owner records show no leak in 15 years and the tank passed a visual check this year.
The utility risk assessment scores the site as its highest source risk because of volume, distance, and the drainage path.
A replacement double wall tank with containment is available under a provincial upgrade program the owner has not applied to.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Visual inspection this year removes the need for containment
No upgrade option exists for the owner
The site is a high consequence source risk despite its clean history, and the upgrade path exists, so engagement on replacement is the supported action
15 years without a leak makes the site low risk

inference.explanation: Risk combines consequence and pathway, not history alone, and the single wall tank with a ditch pathway to the creek scores highest for those reasons. A visual check does not substitute for containment, and an upgrade program exists unapplied.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the high risk ranking?

options.label: Archived owner leak history statement
Archived visual inspection note
Archived site risk assessment scoring volume, distance, containment, and drainage pathway

nextClue.explanation: The correct record directly tests the supported explanation against the alternatives.

clueText.nc-a: Clean history does not change containment or pathway.
clueText.nc-b: The visual check found no leak but no containment either.
clueText.nc-c: The scoring ranks this site highest on pathway and consequence factors.

tasks.prompt: A plant evaluates replacing chlorine contact tank baffles after a decade of disinfection records and a new tracer study.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment utility record. Steady operation unless noted. Archived plant, laboratory, and management records are available for review.

evidence.label: The new tracer study gives a baffling factor of 0.45, the same as the study 10 years ago.
CT compliance has been met every day for 5 years with margin at peak flow in the disinfection log.
Baffle inspection by camera shows curtains intact with minor fouling that cleaning removed.
A vendor proposal claims a new baffle system would raise the factor to 0.70, based on a different tank geometry.
Chlorine dose has been stable and residuals meet targets at current settings.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The vendor factor claim is based on this tank tested geometry
Records show the existing baffles perform as originally measured with compliant CT, so replacement is not supported on performance grounds
Tracer results show baffling has collapsed over 10 years
CT compliance has been failing at peak flow

inference.explanation: The tracer factor is unchanged in 10 years, CT is compliant with margin, and the baffles are intact after cleaning. The vendor figure comes from different geometry, so it does not prove a gain in this tank.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms current baffle performance?

options.label: Archived baffle purchase date
Archived tracer studies 10 years apart paired with the 5 year CT compliance log
Archived vendor proposal

nextClue.explanation: The correct record directly tests the supported explanation against the alternatives.

clueText.nc-a: Purchase date shows age, not performance.
clueText.nc-b: Both tracer studies read 0.45 and CT holds margin at peak flow throughout.
clueText.nc-c: The proposal uses a different tank geometry.

tasks.prompt: Residual chlorine modelling for a growing system is checked against field data before being used for booster station planning.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment utility record. Steady operation unless noted. Archived plant, laboratory, and management records are available for review.

evidence.label: The model predicts far zone residuals within 0.05 mg/L of field values at 12 of 14 validation points.
At the 2 failing points, both downstream of one storage tank, the model over predicts residual by 0.3 mg/L.
Tank records at that site show turnover of 8 days, while the model assumed the design value of 3 days.
Updating the model with measured turnover in a test run brings both points within 0.06 mg/L of field values.
Pipe ages and materials in the model match the asset records for the zone.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The model is sound except for one tank turnover input, and correcting that input validates it for booster planning
The model is unusable everywhere for planning
Pipe data errors explain the two failing points
Field measurements at the two points must be wrong

inference.explanation: Twelve points validate as built, and a single wrong input explains both failures and fixes them in a test run. Pipe data were verified, and two independent field points agreeing against the model point to the model input, not the measurements.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the turnover input error?

options.label: Archived validation table by point paired with measured versus assumed tank turnover and the corrected test run
Archived model software documentation
Archived asset pipe records

nextClue.explanation: The correct record directly tests the supported explanation against the alternatives.

clueText.nc-a: Correcting turnover from 3 to 8 days brings the failing points into agreement.
clueText.nc-b: Documentation does not show site inputs.
clueText.nc-c: Pipe records matched the model, ruling out that cause.

tasks.prompt: A utility reviews whether to insource or contract its regulatory sampling after a cost and quality comparison over 2 years.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment utility record. Steady operation unless noted. Archived plant, laboratory, and management records are available for review.

evidence.label: Contract sampling missed 4 percent of scheduled samples over 2 years, all on statutory holiday weeks.
In house sampling in the prior period missed 1 percent, with misses spread across the year.
Quality audits show equal chain of custody and holding time performance for both options.
Contract cost per sample is 22 percent lower at current volumes, excluding the utility re sampling cost for missed samples.
Including re sampling and staff follow up for misses, the 2 year total costs are within 3 percent of each other.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Contract sampling is 22 percent cheaper in total cost
Quality performance clearly favours the contractor
Missed samples were equal between the options
On total cost the options are nearly equal, so the decision turns on reliability, where in house sampling missed fewer scheduled samples

inference.explanation: The 22 percent figure excludes miss costs and the full totals land within 3 percent, while quality audits are equal. Miss rates differ clearly at 4 percent versus 1 percent, so reliability, not headline price, separates the options.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the total cost picture?

options.label: Archived contract price per sample alone
Archived quality audit summary alone
Archived 2 year total cost comparison including re sampling and follow up, with miss rates by option

nextClue.explanation: The correct record directly tests the supported explanation against the alternatives.

clueText.nc-a: Price per sample omits the miss costs that close the gap.
clueText.nc-b: Quality was equal, so audits do not separate the options.
clueText.nc-c: Totals are within 3 percent once misses are costed, and in house misses are one quarter of contract misses.

tasks.prompt: Finished water pH adjustment is reviewed after corrosion control sampling shows a shift in one of two treatment plants feeding one system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment utility record. Steady operation unless noted. Archived plant, laboratory, and management records are available for review.

evidence.label: Plant A finished pH averages 7.9 and Plant B averages 7.3 after a chemical feed change at Plant B only.
Lead sampling in the Plant B dominant zone rose over two rounds, while the Plant A zone stayed at historic lows.
Alkalinity is matched between the plants, so the pH gap is a dosing difference, not source chemistry.
Restoring Plant B caustic feed to its prior setpoint in a trial returned finished pH to 7.8 within a week.
Distribution pipe materials are similar across both zones per asset records.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Lead results are unrelated to finished pH in this system
Pipe materials differ and fully explain the zone difference
The Plant B feed change lowered its finished pH and tracks the lead rise in its zone, and restoring the setpoint corrects the chemistry
Source chemistry differs between the plants and causes the pH gap

inference.explanation: Alkalinity and sources are matched while only Plant B changed its feed, and the setpoint trial reversed the pH shift. Similar pipe materials rule out the asset explanation, and the timing ties the lead rise to the chemistry change in that zone.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the feed change effect?

options.label: Archived pipe material inventory
Archived Plant B feed setpoint change log paired with finished pH and zone lead trends
Archived source alkalinity results

nextClue.explanation: The correct record directly tests the supported explanation against the alternatives.

clueText.nc-a: Pipe materials are similar across zones.
clueText.nc-b: pH fell after the Plant B change and recovered when the setpoint was restored.
clueText.nc-c: Alkalinity was matched between plants.

tasks.prompt: A long term asset review of raw water intake screens compares cleaning frequency, headloss, and fish impingement records.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment utility record. Steady operation unless noted. Archived plant, laboratory, and management records are available for review.

evidence.label: Screen headloss rises to the cleaning trigger in 9 days during autumn leaf fall and 40 days in winter.
Cleaning on a fixed monthly schedule leaves the screens above the trigger for up to 3 weeks each autumn.
A condition based trial cleaning on headloss trigger held headloss in range all autumn with 5 cleanings.
Pump energy rises 11 percent when screens run above the headloss trigger in the paired records.
Impingement counts meet the environmental approval limits under both schedules.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Condition based cleaning raised impingement above approval limits
Condition based cleaning on headloss keeps screens in range and avoids the energy penalty that the fixed monthly schedule allows each autumn
Fixed monthly cleaning keeps headloss in range all year
Pump energy is unaffected by screen headloss

inference.explanation: Autumn fouling outruns the monthly schedule by weeks, energy rises above the trigger, and the condition based trial held range with limits met. Each alternative claim is directly contradicted by the paired seasonal records.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the condition based case?

options.label: Archived seasonal headloss trend under both schedules paired with pump energy at high headloss
Archived cleaning schedule document
Archived impingement count summary alone

nextClue.explanation: The correct record directly tests the supported explanation against the alternatives.

clueText.nc-a: Headloss stays in range only under trigger based cleaning, and energy rises 11 percent above the trigger.
clueText.nc-b: The schedule document states intent, not results.
clueText.nc-c: Impingement met limits under both schedules.
